content.value_statement: REST APIs need consistent methods, status codes, caching, and rate limits. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code quick patterns for practical API design.
actual_capabilities: Compare HTTP methods, idempotency, and cacheability rules.
Review resource URLs, query parameters, pagination, sorting, and filtering patterns.
Apply Cache-Control, ETag, CDN, and invalidation guidance.
Design rate limit headers, retry handling, tiers, and endpoint limits.
Structure error responses, versioning choices, bulk operations, and HATEOAS links.
limitations: It does not inspect live APIs or call external services.
It does not generate a full framework implementation.
Examples are generic and need project-specific adaptation.
It does not replace a security or privacy review.

use_cases.title: Plan a New API
use_cases.description: Choose resource names, methods, status codes, pagination, caching, and rate limits before implementation.

use_cases.title: Review Endpoint Consistency
use_cases.description: Compare an API contract against common REST patterns and identify inconsistent choices.

use_cases.title: Document Integration Behavior
use_cases.description: Describe status codes, error formats, retry behavior, versioning, and cache semantics clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the rest-patterns skill to choose HTTP methods and status codes for these operations: create, read, update, delete, validation failure, and rate limiting.

prompt_templates.title: Design Collection Endpoints
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the rest-patterns skill to design collection endpoints for this resource. Include pagination, sorting, filtering, sparse fields, and included relationships.

prompt_templates.title: Add Caching and Limits
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the rest-patterns skill to recommend caching headers, ETag behavior, CDN invalidation, and rate limit headers for these API endpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an API Contract
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the rest-patterns skill to review this API contract for method semantics, status code choices, error response shape, versioning, bulk operations, and HATEOAS links.

output_examples.input: I need status codes for create, update, delete, and validation failure.
output_examples.output: Use 201 with Location for create, 200 or 204 for update, 204 for delete, and 422 for validation errors.

output_examples.input: Help me add caching to product catalog endpoints.
output_examples.output: Use public cache headers for stable catalog data, ETags for validation, and no-store for personalized or sensitive responses.

output_examples.input: Review a rate limit policy for free and paid users.
output_examples.output: Define separate tiers, return RateLimit and Retry-After headers, and document retry behavior for clients.

best_practices: Start with resource nouns, standard HTTP methods, and clear collection pagination.
Pair every error response with a stable code, message, and request identifier.
Treat caching, authentication, and rate limits as part of endpoint design.
anti_patterns: Using verbs in URLs instead of method semantics.
Returning 200 for validation, authentication, or authorization failures.
Caching authenticated or sensitive responses without explicit no-store or private controls.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps design REST APIs with consistent methods, status codes, resource paths, caching, rate limits, and response formats.

faq.question: Does this skill make network calls?
faq.answer: No. It provides Markdown reference material and examples for API design decisions.

faq.question: Can it help choose status codes?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for success, redirect, client error, and server error status codes.

faq.question: Does it cover rate limiting?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers common headers, retry behavior, limit tiers, endpoint limits, and client backoff patterns.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Should I copy the examples directly?
faq.answer: Use them as patterns. Adapt names, limits, headers, and error details to your API contract.
